articles.title: Home Assistant’s web terminal opens to screen readers
articles.dek: Typing and command output become readable without changing the terminal’s appearance.
body: The Terminal & SSH app makes Home Assistant’s web terminal readable by screen readers. Previously, its canvas-based display left assistive software with an empty page instead of the commands being typed and the output they produced.

The accessible mode starts enabled for everyone, so a screen-reader user does not have to find a setting inside an inaccessible terminal. Its appearance stays the same. Can K. checked typing, command output and the status line with JAWS and NVDA on Windows, including a local Home Assistant OS installation.

Large bursts of output still reach the terminal’s announcement limit after about twenty lines, after which the rows can be read manually. This is Can K.’s first contribution to the Terminal & SSH repository.

pullRequests.title: Enable screen reader mode in the web terminal

articles.title: Music Assistant builds in music controls for AI assistants
articles.dek: A discoverable connection provides search, playback and queue tools without a separate community plugin.
body: Music Assistant adds a built-in connection for AI assistants to find music, choose players and manage playback. It uses the Model Context Protocol, the interface used by assistants such as Claude and ChatGPT, and provides fifteen tools covering searching, queues, favourites, playlists and speaker grouping.

When Music Assistant runs as a Home Assistant app, it announces the connection for discovery in Home Assistant. Other clients connect using a Music Assistant token, and commands respect the calling account’s role and player access. The older community plugin remains separately identified.

The server also prepares for Home Assistant to pass along the person making a request. That part requires a corresponding Home Assistant change; it does not yet establish per-person identity forwarding from Assist.

pullRequests.title: Builtin MCP server for AI assistants and Home Assistant
Let Home Assistant discover the built-in MCP server
Use the reverse-DNS _meta key for the Home Assistant user in MCP tool calls

articles.title: Device buyers ask for clearer compatibility and local-control information
articles.dek: The October research snapshot records priorities from 740 participants, with a strong European and technical skew.
body: The Open Home Foundation’s October device-database survey snapshot finds people looking for clearer answers before buying smart-home hardware. Of 740 respondents, 652 selected pre-purchase research as a use for the database. Local control was a critical device attribute for 631, close behind communication protocols at 657.

The gaps mirror those priorities. Unclear compatibility information was selected by 496 respondents, while 476 wanted better information about local control. Those questions allowed multiple choices, so the counts overlap.

The snapshot is dated October 15 and adds 25 responses to August’s total. Its participants are mostly technically experienced, and 551 are based in Europe. These findings describe that survey sample rather than every smart-home household.

pullRequests.title: october 2026 survey results

articles.title: E3/DC home batteries gain a local Home Assistant connection
articles.dek: The new integration reads household power flows and battery status over the home network.
body: Home Assistant adds a local connection to E3/DC home power stations through Modbus TCP. The initial integration reports power flowing through solar panels, the battery, the house, the grid, additional feeders and wallboxes.
It also reads battery charge, self-sufficiency, self-consumption and emergency-power status. This first step provides readings and connection setup; it does not add battery or charging controls.

pullRequests.title: Add E3/DC Modbus TCP integration

articles.title: Music Assistant shows who maintains an integration
articles.dek: Community badges and a Get help button direct questions to the people responsible.
body: Music Assistant marks community-maintained integrations and names their maintainers when someone adds or opens one. The labels distinguish those projects from integrations maintained by the Music Assistant team.

Each integration page gets a Get help button. It opens the maintainer’s support destination when one is supplied, or starts a report in Music Assistant’s support repository with the integration already identified.

articles.title: ESPHome configures and monitors BQ25820 solar chargers
articles.dek: A new driver exposes charging settings, battery readings and faults for makers building with Texas Instruments’ controller.
body: ESPHome adds support for the Texas Instruments BQ25820 battery charger. Makers can configure charging limits and the controller’s solar power tracking over its wired connection, then read battery and input voltage, current, charging state and faults.

The driver restores its settings after the chip resets or its watchdog expires, and retries a configuration that could not be written. Ashley Theiss makes a first contribution to ESPHome with the addition.

BQ25820 component documentation

articles.title: Device Builder restores free pins on imported ESPHome boards
articles.dek: The pin picker stops treating every connection as occupied on hundreds of imported board definitions.
body: ESPHome Device Builder restores unused pins to board definitions imported from the device catalogue. Those definitions often listed only the pins already used by built-in parts, leaving the picker with nothing free to offer when a maker added another component.

The importer fills out the chip’s pin list while retaining the board’s occupied pins, and preserves wired buses needed by components outside the catalogue. The reported failure on an M5StickC PLUS left every I²C pin choice unavailable, preventing setup of its onboard motion sensor.

pullRequests.title: Offer free pins on imported boards and keep their unconsumed buses

articles.title: Home Assistant stops area controls freezing large dashboards
articles.dek: Room controls inspect their own entities instead of repeatedly scanning the whole installation.
body: Home Assistant corrects a dashboard freeze affecting large installations with several area cards. Every state change could make each control type scan all entities, multiplying the work across cards.
The controls first find the entities in their own area and repeat that lookup only when the device and entity registries change. The area overview and controls editor use the same approach.

pullRequests.title: Fix area controls freezing large dashboards

articles.title: Home Assistant prevents one bad setting from freezing MQTT updates
articles.dek: An invalid text encoding can no longer interrupt readings for other MQTT devices.
body: Home Assistant prevents a bad MQTT text-encoding setting from stopping updates for other devices. A subscription covering every topic could previously interrupt all MQTT entity updates without writing an error to the log.

Unknown encoding names are rejected when entities, discovery messages and triggers are configured. If an invalid encoding still reaches the receiving code, that subscription is logged and skipped while other subscribers continue.

pullRequests.title: Validate the MQTT payload encoding and handle an unknown encoding on receive

articles.title: UniFi readings create fewer Home Assistant history entries
articles.dek: Routine CPU, memory and temperature changes slow down while larger jumps still appear immediately.
body: Home Assistant reduces history entries from UniFi devices that report changing CPU, memory and temperature values every few seconds. Routine changes wait at least fifteen seconds between readings, while larger jumps are recorded immediately.

In a replay of seven days from Ivan Alekseev’s Cloud Gateway Fiber, CPU records fell from 1,742 to 507 per hour and memory records from 2,299 to 223. Reconnection and availability changes still appear immediately. The measurements describe that gateway, not a guaranteed reduction for every UniFi installation. This is Ivan Alekseev’s first contribution to Home Assistant Core.

pullRequests.title: Limit how often UniFi device CPU, memory and temperature sensors update

articles.title: ESPHome preserves saved MQTT commands when devices connect
articles.dek: Pacing subscriptions prevents an ESP32’s startup burst from dropping switch commands and message triggers.
body: ESPHome keeps an ESP32 from losing retained MQTT messages when it connects with many subscriptions. These messages hold the broker’s last saved value. A busy startup could previously overflow the incoming queue, leaving switches and message-triggered automations without their saved state until another message arrived.

On an ESP32-C3 test with 25 message topics and 15 switch-command topics, the correction delivered every retained message across 28 boots using a nearby access point. Very broad wildcard subscriptions or unusually large messages can still overflow the queue.

pullRequests.title: [mqtt] Keep retained messages from overflowing the ESP32 event queue at connect

articles.title: ESPHome builds firmware for Nordic’s nRF54 development boards
articles.dek: The nRF54LM20 and nRF54L15 kits gain support alongside a J-Link flashing path.
body: ESPHome adds build support for Nordic’s nRF54LM20 and nRF54L15 development kits. Makers can upload firmware through a SEGGER J-Link debugger, which resets the chip afterward so the new program starts.
The J-Link software must be installed separately. The contributor tested both development kits. USB on the nRF54LM20 kit remains a known limitation in this change.

pullRequests.title: [nrf52] Add nRF54LM20/NRF54L15 support and J-Link upload
[nrf52] Document nRF54LM20 DK support and J-Link upload

articles.title: Home Assistant Cast gives up administrator rights
articles.dek: Existing Cast accounts move to ordinary user access while retaining dashboard controls.
body: Home Assistant removes administrator rights from the account used by Home Assistant Cast. New Cast accounts use the ordinary users group, and existing administrator accounts move to it during setup.
Cast only needs to read dashboards and run their actions. Its account keeps remote access because a Cast device may connect through the cloud address.

pullRequests.title: Remove admin rights from the Home Assistant Cast user

articles.title: Offline SimpliSafe sensors stop looking like closed doors
articles.dek: Home Assistant marks an individual disconnected sensor unavailable instead of keeping its last state.
body: Home Assistant marks a SimpliSafe V3 sensor unavailable when SimpliSafe reports that sensor offline. An entry sensor could previously keep showing its last closed state even after it lost contact.
The reading returns on the next update after the device comes back online. This check applies to V3 sensors, rather than cameras or only the alarm system’s overall connection.

pullRequests.title: Mark SimpliSafe sensors unavailable when reported offline

articles.title: Sendspin limits audio requests that can exhaust server memory
articles.dek: The Python library bounds decoding work and releases unused audio encoders.
body: Sendspin’s Python server limits the audio work a connected client can demand. A small compressed FLAC chunk could previously expand to more than a gigabyte of audio, while repeated format changes could leave unused encoders consuming memory.

The library rejects oversized source formats and audio sent too far ahead of real time, checks compressed chunks before decoding, and drops encoders no speaker uses. These protections apply to applications using the Python library; they do not establish an update in every Sendspin product.

pullRequests.title: Bound the audio a source can make the server decode
Free encoders no player uses
Limit player formats to 384 kHz

articles.title: ESPHome stops failed sensor reads becoming zero-degree temperatures
articles.dek: DS248x bridge recovery also avoids sending commands to the wrong sensor channel.
body: ESPHome stops a failed read through a DS248x bridge from appearing as a valid 0°C temperature. When the bridge could not select the requested sensor channel, returned zero bytes could pass the temperature sensor’s error check and become a misleading reading.
The bridge also recovers from temporary communication faults instead of remaining failed until a reboot. Commands wait while recovery restores the chip’s settings.

pullRequests.title: [ds248x] Fix stale channel cache and skip buses on a failed hub

articles.title: Assist expands Bulgarian controls for fans and timers
articles.dek: New phrases select climate fan modes and extend a named or room-specific timer.
body: Assist’s Bulgarian sentence library adds commands for selecting a climate device’s fan mode by name, room or floor, or for the current room. The additions cover settings such as automatic, low and high using Bulgarian phrasing.

Bulgarian speakers also gain more ways to extend timers with combined hours, minutes and seconds, activate a scene in a named room, and press a button entity. These are additions to the command library rather than a new speech-recognition model.

pullRequests.title: Add bg coverage for 12 remaining slot combinations

articles.title: Home Assistant removes its defunct Crownstone connection
articles.dek: The cloud service behind the integration has shut down.
body: Home Assistant removes its Crownstone integration after the cloud service it depended on shut down. The removal also takes out the integration’s documentation.
